# Tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1

## 1. Identity, sequence & evolution

### Identity, Sequence & Evolution of Murine ABL1 (UniProt P00520)

### Gene and Protein Identifiers

The canonical sequence of UniProtKB P00520 corresponds to the mouse (*Mus musculus*) **Abl1** gene product, tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1 (EC 2.7.10.2), also known as Abelson murine leukemia viral oncogene homolog 1, Abelson tyrosine-protein kinase 1, proto-oncogene c-Abl, or p150 [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). The gene symbol is *Abl1* with synonym *Abl*; the mouse gene is the ortholog of the human *ABL1* (UniProt P00519) and of the viral oncogene v-abl carried by Abelson murine leukemia virus [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). The entry is reviewed (Swiss-Prot) and the canonical isoform I is 1,123 amino acids long [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520).

### Isoforms and Mature-Chain Numbering

UniProt lists four isoforms generated by alternative splicing [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520):

- **Isoform I (P00520-1)**: 1,123 aa; the displayed canonical sequence.
- **Isoform II (P00520-2)**: described, sequence VSP_004959.
- **Isoform III (P00520-3)**: described, sequence VSP_004958.
- **Isoform IV (P00520-4)**: described, sequence VSP_004960.

The isoform numbering is UniProt-specific and does not correspond to the historical "1a/1b" nomenclature used in human ABL1 literature. All residue numbers in this chapter refer to the canonical isoform I (P00520-1) unless stated otherwise. No cleaved signal peptide or propeptide is annotated; the protein is not secreted, and the N-terminus is subject to myristoylation (see below), so the mature chain is the full-length polypeptide.

### Sequence Composition and Physicochemical Properties

ProtParam calculations on the canonical 1,123-residue sequence give a molecular weight of 122,671.13 Da, theoretical pI 8.858, GRAVY −0.6256, instability index 57.66 (heuristic, indicating a predicted unstable protein), and aromaticity 0.0641 [S25](https://biopython.org/docs/latest/api/Bio.SeqUtils.ProtParam.html). Amino acid counts are dominated by Ser (126), Ala (95), Leu (94), Pro (93), Glu (90), Lys (81), Gly (79), Arg (67), Thr (67), and Val (53); Cys (18) and Trp (13) are the least abundant [S25](https://biopython.org/docs/latest/api/Bio.SeqUtils.ProtParam.html). The basic pI reflects the arginine/lysine content and is consistent with a nuclear/cytosolic nucleic-acid-binding protein.

### Domain Architecture

InterPro annotation (13 entries) defines the following domains and features in P00520 [S27](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/protein/UniProt/P00520/):

- **SH3 domain**: residues 61–121 (IPR001452; Pfam PF00018; SMART SM00326), with the SH3-like superfamily extending to 62–147 (IPR036028).
- **SH2 domain**: residues 125–217 (IPR000980; Pfam PF00017/PF21990; SMART SM00252); the ABL-specific SH2 domain (CDD cd09935) is mapped to 123–216 (IPR035837); the SH2 superfamily spans 118–262 (IPR036860).
- **Protein kinase domain (tyrosine kinase)**: residues 242–493 (IPR000719; Pfam PF00069; SMART SM00220), also annotated as serine/threonine-tyrosine kinase catalytic domain 242–492 (IPR001245; Pfam PF07714) and tyrosine kinase catalytic domain 242–493 (IPR020635; SMART SM00219). The protein kinase-like superfamily spans 231–498 (IPR011009).
- **ATP binding site**: residues 248–271 (IPR017441; PROSITE PS00107).
- **Tyrosine kinase active site**: residues 359–371 (IPR008266; PROSITE PS00109).
- **F-actin binding domain (FABD)**: residues 997–1123 (IPR015015; Pfam PF08919; SMART SM00808).

The domain order (SH3–SH2–kinase–FABD) is the canonical architecture of the ABL family and is conserved from invertebrates to mammals. The kinase domain contains the canonical DFG motif and the tyrosine kinase active-site signature HRDLAARN (residues ~359–371).

### Post-Translational Modifications and Functional Residues

Key modified residues annotated in UniProt include [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520):

- **Myristoylation** at the N-terminal Gly (by similarity to human), required for membrane association and autoinhibition.
- **Acetylation** at Lys-710 by EP300, promoting cytoplasmic translocation.
- **Phosphorylation** at Tyr-70 (SRC-family kinases; disrupts SH3 autoinhibition), Tyr-226 and Tyr-393 (activation-associated), Ser-446 (ATM-dependent, DNA damage response), Thr-547 and Ser-569 (CDC2-associated kinase, cell-cycle coupled), Ser-618 and Ser-619 (PAK2), and Thr-734 (14-3-3 binding, cytoplasmic sequestration).

These sites are numbered on the mouse isoform I sequence; the corresponding human residues differ slightly in numbering due to length differences in the linker regions.

### Homologs, Orthologs, and Family Evolution

ABL1 belongs to the ABL family of non-receptor tyrosine kinases, which in vertebrates comprises ABL1 and ABL2 (ARG). The mouse Abl1 is the direct ortholog of human ABL1 (P00519), sharing ~95% sequence identity over the full length; the SH3-SH2-kinase cassette is nearly identical, while the C-terminal half shows more divergence. The *Abl1* gene is conserved across Bilateria; *Drosophila* has a single Abl ortholog, and *C. elegans* has two (ABL-1). The viral oncogene v-abl is a truncated, constitutively active form of the murine c-abl captured by the Abelson murine leukemia virus, hence the historical name.

The ABL family is part of the larger SRC/ABL branch of the tyrosine kinase superfamily, sharing the SH3-SH2-kinase domain arrangement with SRC-family kinases but distinguished by a long C-terminal extension containing nuclear localization signals, DNA-binding regions, and the F-actin binding domain. The F-actin binding domain (IPR015015) is unique to ABL family members and is not found in SRC kinases, reflecting ABL's dual nuclear/cytoskeletal functions.

### Conservation and Functional Implications

The high conservation of the SH3-SH2-kinase module across ABL orthologs underscores its central role in autoinhibition and signaling. The N-terminal myristoyl group, the SH3-SH2 linker, and the SH2-kinase interface cooperate to maintain the inactive conformation; mutations disrupting this autoinhibited state (e.g., in the linker or SH3 domain) are oncogenic in human leukemias. The C-terminal F-actin binding domain is essential for ABL's role in cytoskeletal remodeling and is conserved from *Drosophila* to mammals.

### Experimental Structure Evidence

The SH3 domain of mouse ABL1 has been determined by X-ray crystallography at 2.0 Å resolution in complex with a synthetic peptide from 3BP-1 (PDB 1ABO) [S41](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1ABO). The structure comprises residues ~62–121 of the SH3 domain (62 residues in the polymer) and demonstrates the canonical SH3 fold with a peptide-binding groove. This provides direct experimental evidence for the SH3 domain boundaries and its ligand-binding surface.

### Model Predictions (Not Experimental Validation)

ESM2-650M-based predictors provide supplementary, non-validated estimates: solubility class 1 (prob. 0.906) [S33]; subcellular localization predicted as class 4 (prob. 0.484) with a second class at 0.474, consistent with the known nuclear/cytoplasmic distribution [S34]; non-membrane protein (prob. 0.733) [S35]; no metal-ion binding (prob. 0.613) [S36]; thermostability score 0.336 [S37]; no canonical sorting signal [S38]. These predictions are consistent with the annotated biology but do not constitute experimental evidence.

### Gaps and Caveats

- The exact sequences of isoforms II–IV are not provided in the source; their lengths and domain compositions are not independently verified here.
- The N-terminal myristoylation and the precise start of the mature chain are inferred by similarity to human ABL1, not directly demonstrated in mouse.
- The functional significance of isoform-specific differences in the C-terminal region remains incompletely characterized.
- No experimental structure of the full-length mouse ABL1 is available; domain boundaries are inferred from sequence homology and the isolated SH3 domain structure.

## 2. Function, catalysis & pathways

### Function, Catalysis & Pathways of Murine ABL1 (P00520)

### Catalytic Activity and Enzyme Classification

Murine ABL1 (UniProt P00520) is a non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase classified under EC 2.7.10.2, catalyzing the reaction: **L-tyrosyl-[protein] + ATP → O-phospho-L-tyrosyl-[protein] + ADP + H⁺** (RHEA:10596) [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). This activity is supported by experimental evidence from multiple publications (PubMed IDs 10988075, 12748290, 19878872, 20072125) and by PROSITE-ProRule PRU10028 [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). The enzyme transfers the γ-phosphate of ATP to the phenolic hydroxyl group of specific tyrosine residues on substrate proteins.

### Domain Architecture Relevant to Catalysis

The catalytic machinery of ABL1 is organized into several functional domains [S27](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/protein/UniProt/P00520/):

- **SH3 domain** (residues 61–121): mediates protein-protein interactions and participates in autoinhibition
- **SH2 domain** (residues 125–217): binds phosphotyrosine-containing motifs; also contributes to the autoinhibitory clamp
- **Kinase domain** (residues 242–493): contains the bilobal catalytic core
  - ATP-binding site: residues 248–271 (glycine-rich P-loop)
  - Active site signature: residues 359–371
  - Tyrosine-protein kinase active site: residues 359–371 (PROSITE PS00109)
- **F-actin binding domain** (residues 997–1123): links kinase signaling to cytoskeletal regulation

The kinase domain exhibits the canonical bilobal architecture: an N-lobe containing the glycine-rich phosphate-binding loop (P-loop) essential for ATP binding and the αC helix, and a C-lobe providing the substrate-binding surface. The active site sits between these lobes and encompasses the activation loop (A-loop) and ATP-binding pocket [S44](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12064879). The A-loop contains Tyr-393 (equivalent to Tyr-412 in human ABL1 numbering used in some literature), an essential autophosphorylation site that switches the kinase between active and inactive conformations [S44](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12064879).

### Cofactor Requirements

ABL1 requires a divalent metal cation for catalysis. Experimental evidence (PubMed 12748290) demonstrates that **Mg²⁺** (ChEBI:18420) serves as the cofactor [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). The original kinase assays employed buffers containing both Mg²⁺ and Mn²⁺, but Mg²⁺ is considered the physiologically relevant cofactor [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). The metal ion coordinates the phosphate groups of ATP, stabilizing the transition state and facilitating phosphoryl transfer.

### Enzyme Mechanism and Activation

### Autoinhibited State

ABL1 is stabilized in an inactive conformation through multiple intramolecular interactions [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520):
1. Association between the SH3 domain and the SH2-kinase linker region
2. Interactions of the N-terminal cap
3. Contributions from an N-terminal myristoyl group and phospholipids

This autoinhibited state prevents premature substrate phosphorylation and maintains low basal activity.

### Activation Mechanisms

Several pathways lead to kinase activation [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520):

- **Autophosphorylation**: ABL1 undergoes autophosphorylation, particularly at Tyr-393 within the activation loop, stabilizing the active conformation [S44](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12064879)
- **SRC-family kinase phosphorylation**: Phosphorylation at Tyr-70 by SRC family members disrupts SH3 domain-based autoinhibitory interactions and enhances kinase activity
- **RIN1 binding**: Interaction with RIN1 through the SH2 and SH3 domains activates the kinase
- **DNA damage signals**: Cell death inducers and DNA-damage agents stimulate ABL1 activity
- **Phosphorylation at Tyr-226 and Tyr-393**: Correlates with increased activity

### Inhibitory Regulation

- **Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2)**: Inhibits tyrosine kinase activity
- **Imatinib mesylate (Gleevec)**: A competitive inhibitor at the ATP-binding site
- **14-3-3 proteins**: Sequester ABL1 in the cytoplasm following phosphorylation at Thr-734

### Substrate Specificity and Phosphorylation Targets

ABL1 phosphorylates a diverse array of substrates involved in distinct cellular processes [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520):

### Cytoskeletal Regulation
- **WASF3**: phosphorylation critical for lamellipodia formation and cell migration
- **ANXA1**: membrane anchoring
- **DBN1, DBNL, CTTN, RAPH1, ENAH**: signaling in cytoskeletal dynamics
- **MAPT, PXN**: microtubule-binding proteins

### Cell Adhesion and Motility
- **BCAR1, CRK, CRKL, DOK1, EFS, NEDD9**: key regulators of adhesion and motility
- Phosphorylation of NEDD9/HEF1 is induced by CXCL12 stimulation and promotes T-cell migration, polarization, and homing

### Receptor Endocytosis
- **EGFR**: phosphorylation promotes endocytosis
- **MUSK**: facilitates neuromuscular synapse formation
- **PDGFRB**: phosphorylation inhibits chemotaxis
- **CAV1 (caveolin) and RIN1**: endocytosis regulation
- **CBL family ubiquitin ligases**: phosphorylation leads to increased EGFR stability

### DNA Damage Response and Apoptosis
- **DDB1, DDB2, ERCC3, ERCC6, RAD9A, RAD51, RAD52, WRN**: DNA repair mediators
- **TP73**: primary regulator of damage-induced apoptosis
- **CASP9**: phosphorylated at Tyr-191 (murine numbering; Tyr-153 in some isoform numbering), regulating its processing in the apoptotic response
- **PSMA7**: phosphorylation inhibits proteasomal activity, blocking cell cycle transitions

### Immune Regulation
- **TBX21**: phosphorylation enhances its transcriptional activator activity, regulating T-cell differentiation
- **NEDD9/HEF1 and RAP1**: activation promotes chemokine-mediated T-cell functions

### Autophagy
- **STX17**: probable phosphorylation target involved in late-stage autophagy
- Regulation of lysosomal component trafficking and function

### Kinetics and Assay Conditions

Detailed kinetic parameters (Km, kcat, Vmax) for murine ABL1 are not provided in the reviewed sources. The experimental evidence for catalytic activity derives from assays using:
- Kinase buffers containing both Mg²⁺ and Mn²⁺ [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520)
- Peptide or protein substrates with tyrosine residues
- ATP as phosphate donor

The lack of quantitative kinetic constants in the available literature represents a significant gap. Published studies (e.g., PubMed 12748290) established the EC number through direct enzymatic assays but did not report detailed steady-state parameters in the reviewed annotation.

### Cellular Localization and Compartmentalization

ABL1 exhibits dynamic subcellular localization that is intimately tied to its function [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520):

- **Nucleus**: The myristoylated c-ABL protein is reported to be nuclear, where it participates in DNA damage responses
- **Cytoplasm/cytoskeleton**: Sequestered into the cytoplasm through interaction with 14-3-3 proteins (requires Thr-734 phosphorylation); associates with actin cytoskeleton
- **Mitochondrion**: Localizes to mitochondria in response to oxidative stress, mediating mitochondrial dysfunction and cell death

Acetylation at Lys-710 by EP300 promotes cytoplasmic translocation [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). The nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling is critical for ABL1's dual roles in DNA damage signaling (nuclear) and cytoskeletal regulation (cytoplasmic).

### Expression Patterns

ABL1 is **widely expressed** across tissues [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). The gene produces at least four isoforms through alternative splicing (isoforms I–IV), with isoform I (P00520-1, 1123 residues) serving as the displayed reference sequence [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Isoform-specific functions and expression patterns are not detailed in the reviewed sources.

### Pathway Involvement

Reactome pathway annotations (inferred for Mus musculus) place ABL1 in ten signaling pathways [S30](https://reactome.org/ContentService/data/mapping/UniProt/P00520/pathways):

1. **Regulation of actin dynamics for phagocytic cup formation** (R-MMU-2029482)
2. **Role of ABL in ROBO-SLIT signaling** (R-MMU-428890)
3. **Myogenesis** (R-MMU-525793)
4. **RHO GTPases activate WASPs and WAVEs** (R-MMU-5663213)
5. **HDR through Single Strand Annealing** (R-MMU-5685938)
6. **Recruitment and ATM-mediated phosphorylation of repair proteins at DNA double-strand breaks** (R-MMU-5693565)
7. **Cyclin D associated events in G1** (R-MMU-69231)
8. **RUNX1 regulation of HSC differentiation genes** (R-MMU-8939236)
9. **MLL4/MLL3 regulation of PPARG target genes** (R-MMU-9841922)
10. **Shear stress signaling by PIEZO1 and integrins in endothelial cells** (R-MMU-9860927)

These pathway annotations are inferred from human ortholog data and should be interpreted as predicted rather than directly experimentally validated in mouse.

### Gene Ontology Annotations

QuickGO provides 320 total annotations for P00520, with 25 retrieved in the truncated response [S28](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/annotations?geneProductId=P00520). Key biological process annotations include:
- **GO:0001843** (neural tube closure) - IGI evidence
- **GO:0001922** (B-1 B cell homeostasis) - IMP
- **GO:0002322** (B cell proliferation) - IMP/IGI
- **GO:0006909** (phagocytosis) - IMP/IGI
- **GO:0006979** (response to oxidative stress) - ISO/IMP
- **GO:0007173** (EGF receptor signaling) - IGI
- **GO:0018108** (peptidyl-tyrosine phosphorylation) - IDA
- **GO:0030035** (actin cytoskeleton reorganization) - IDA
- **GO:0030514** (negative regulation of BMP signaling) - IMP

### Pathogen Subversion

ABL1 kinase signaling is hijacked by multiple pathogens to reorganize host actin cytoskeleton [S45](https://www.abcam.com/en-us/targets/abl1/7576). Documented microbial substrates include:
- **A36R** of Vaccinia virus
- **Tir** (translocated intimin receptor) of pathogenic E. coli and possibly Citrobacter
- **CagA** (cytotoxin-associated gene A) of H. pylori
- **AnkA** (ankyrin repeat-containing protein A) of A. phagocytophilum

This highlights ABL1's role at the host-pathogen interface, though detailed mechanistic studies in murine systems are limited.

### Structural Evidence

The crystal structure of the ABL SH3 domain complexed with a 3BP-1 synthetic peptide (PDB: 1ABO) was determined by X-ray diffraction at 2.0 Å resolution [S41](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1ABO). This structure (deposited 1994, primary citation Musacchio et al., Nat Struct Biol 1994) provides atomic-level details of SH3 domain-peptide recognition relevant to substrate targeting. The structure contains 62 residues of the SH3 domain (molecular weight 6.88 kDa) complexed with a 10-residue peptide.

### Sequence-Derived Properties

The 1123-residue isoform I has a calculated molecular weight of 122,671.13 Da, theoretical pI of 8.86, and GRAVY score of -0.626, indicating hydrophilic character [S25](https://biopython.org/docs/latest/api/Bio.SeqUtils.ProtParam.html). The instability index (57.7) suggests intrinsic instability, consistent with a tightly regulated signaling kinase. Amino acid composition shows enrichment in serine (126 residues), proline (93), alanine (95), and leucine (94), with 30 tyrosine residues available as potential phosphorylation sites [S25](https://biopython.org/docs/latest/api/Bio.SeqUtils.ProtParam.html).

### Gaps and Limitations

Several important gaps exist in the reviewed evidence:

1. **Quantitative kinetics**: No Km, kcat, or Vmax values for murine ABL1 were reported in the sources
2. **Isoform-specific functions**: The four splice isoforms' differential catalytic activities, substrate preferences, and tissue distributions remain unspecified
3. **Murine-specific substrates**: Many substrate annotations derive from human ABL1 (P00519) by similarity, requiring experimental validation in mouse
4. **Pathway evidence**: Reactome annotations are inferred from human data; direct experimental confirmation in murine systems is lacking for most pathways
5. **Kinetic comparison**: No direct comparison of murine versus human ABL1 enzymatic properties was available

The distinction between experimentally validated murine functions (e.g., TBX21 phosphorylation, NEDD9 activation) and those inferred from human orthologs (marked "By similarity" in UniProt) should be maintained when interpreting ABL1 biology.

## 3. Structure, dynamics & ligand binding

### Structure, Dynamics & Ligand Binding of Murine ABL1 (P00520)

### Domain Architecture and Sequence Features

Murine ABL1 (UniProt P00520) is a 1,123-residue non-receptor tyrosine kinase (EC 2.7.10.2) with a calculated molecular weight of 122.7 kDa and theoretical pI of 8.86 [S25](https://biopython.org/docs/latest/api/Bio.SeqUtils.ProtParam.html). The protein exhibits a strongly hydrophilic character (GRAVY −0.626) and a high predicted instability index (57.7), consistent with a multi-domain signaling protein containing substantial intrinsically disordered regions [S25](https://biopython.org/docs/latest/api/Bio.SeqUtils.ProtParam.html). InterPro annotation defines the canonical domain organization: an SH3 domain (residues 61–121), SH2 domain (residues 125–217), and tyrosine kinase catalytic domain (residues 242–493), with the kinase domain belonging to the protein kinase-like superfamily (residues 231–498) [S27](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/protein/UniProt/P00520/). The C-terminal region contains an F-actin binding domain (residues 997–1123) [S27](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/protein/UniProt/P00520/). The ATP-binding site maps to residues 248–271 and the tyrosine kinase active-site signature to residues 359–371 [S27](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/protein/UniProt/P00520/).

Four isoforms arise from alternative splicing (P00520-1 through P00520-4), with lengths of 1,123, 1,117, 1,118, and 1,142 residues respectively [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Isoform-specific sequence differences occur primarily in the N-terminal region, which may affect myristoylation and membrane targeting.

### Experimental Structures and Coverage

PDBe mapping identifies 45 experimental structures covering murine ABL1, all determined by X-ray diffraction [S32](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/api/mappings/best_structures/P00520). The most comprehensive structure is PDB 1OPK, covering residues 27–515 (43.5% of the full-length protein) at 1.8 Å resolution [S32](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/api/mappings/best_structures/P00520). The kinase domain (residues 229–515) is represented by numerous high-resolution structures, including 3KFA at 1.22 Å (the highest resolution available), 3K5V at 1.74 Å, 1OPJ at 1.75 Å, and 3MS9 at 1.8 Å [S32](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/api/mappings/best_structures/P00520). Multiple structures at ~1.9–2.0 Å resolution include 3KF4, 2QOH, 2Z60, 3MSS, and 6HD4 [S32](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/api/mappings/best_structures/P00520). These structures typically contain two chains (A and B) in the asymmetric unit, with 3MSS containing four chains [S32](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/api/mappings/best_structures/P00520).

The SH3 domain has been structurally characterized in complex with a synthetic peptide from 3BP-1 (PDB 1ABO), determined at 2.0 Å resolution [S41](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1ABO). This structure contains the SH3 domain (62 residues) bound to a 10-residue peptide, with two copies of the complex in the asymmetric unit and 121 solvent atoms modeled [S41](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1ABO). The structure reveals the canonical SH3 fold with a peptide-binding groove recognizing proline-rich motifs.

No experimental structure covers the full-length protein; the C-terminal region (residues 516–1123) lacks experimental structural coverage in the deposited datasets [S32](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/api/mappings/best_structures/P00520).

### Oligomerization and Intermolecular Interfaces

The crystal structures of the kinase domain consistently show two molecules per asymmetric unit [S32](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/api/mappings/best_structures/P00520), suggesting possible dimerization interfaces, though this may reflect crystal packing rather than physiological oligomerization. The SH3 domain structure 1ABO contains two protein chains plus two peptide chains per asymmetric unit, with an assembly count of three in the entry [S41](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1ABO).

UniProt documents extensive intermolecular interactions relevant to structure-function relationships [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). The SH3 domain mediates direct interaction with CASP9, and the SH2/SH3 region binds RIN1, which activates ABL1. IntAct-curated interactions include associations with CDON, DOK1, NCK1, PSTPIP1, and SNCA in mouse, plus cross-species interactions with CDKN1B, EPHB2, and PTPN18 [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). A specific interaction between isoform 4 (P00520-4) and ABI1 is documented with five experiments [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520).

### Ligand Binding and Regulatory Mechanisms

The kinase domain binds ATP and Mg²⁺, with Mg²⁺ identified as the likely in vivo cofactor based on experimental evidence [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). The catalytic activity transfers phosphate from ATP to L-tyrosyl-[protein] substrates [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520).

Autoinhibition involves multiple elements: the SH3 domain associates with the SH2-kinase linker, the N-terminal cap contributes to stabilization, and an N-terminal myristoyl group plus phospholipids maintain the inactive conformation [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) inhibits kinase activity. Imatinib mesylate (Gleevec) is a documented inhibitor [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Activation occurs through autophosphorylation, SRC-family kinase phosphorylation, or RIN1 binding to SH2/SH3 domains [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520).

Phosphorylation sites with structural implications include Tyr-70 (SRC family phosphorylation disrupting SH3-based autoinhibitory interactions), Tyr-226 and Tyr-393 (correlating with increased activity), Ser-446 (ATM-dependent, required for DNA damage activation), and Thr-547/Ser-569 (CDC2-associated kinase, coupled to cell division) [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Phosphorylation at Ser-618/Ser-619 by PAK2 modulates binding preferences between CRK and ABI1 [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Acetylation at Lys-710 by EP300 promotes cytoplasmic translocation [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520).

### Conformational States and Dynamics

The inactive conformation is stabilized by intramolecular associations between SH3 and the SH2-kinase linker, the N-terminal cap, and myristoyl group interactions [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Foldseek structural similarity searches identify the closest experimental match as PDB 2FO0, the SH3-SH2 unit of human c-Abl in active and inactive forms (99.5% sequence identity over residues 19–466), providing a structural template for understanding conformational transitions [S26](https://search.foldseek.com/result/9iaZKGInqYU4-QKHHPSvwQ_lrqIVyLmeBHHXiA/0).

Molecular dynamics studies (referenced via PDB 6BL8) have explored conformational variability of the Abl kinase domain, with Markov state models used to characterize the conformational landscape [S26](https://search.foldseek.com/result/9iaZKGInqYU4-QKHHPSvwQ_lrqIVyLmeBHHXiA/0). These analyses are relevant to understanding how the kinase transitions between inactive and active states and how mutations or inhibitors shift conformational equilibria.

### Predicted Structures and Disorder

AlphaFold DB provides four predicted models corresponding to the four isoforms [S31](https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P00520). The full-length isoform 1 model (AF-P00520-F1) has a global pLDDT of 63.44, with 49.1% of residues in the very low confidence category (pLDDT < 50) and only modest fractions in low-confidence ranges [S31](https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P00520). This pattern indicates that large portions of the protein—particularly the C-terminal half—are predicted to be disordered or lack stable tertiary structure. Isoform 2 (AF-P00520-2-F1) has a slightly higher global score (64.69) with 47.7% very low confidence residues; isoform 3 (AF-P00520-3-F1) scores 63.97; isoform 4 (AF-P00520-4-F1) scores 62.84 [S31](https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P00520).

The N-terminal region (approximately residues 1–500) is predicted with high confidence, consistent with the availability of experimental structures for this region. The C-terminal region beyond the kinase domain is predicted to be largely disordered, which aligns with the absence of experimental structures and the known intrinsically disordered nature of Abl family C-termini. Foldseek comparisons show that the predicted N-terminal region (residues 1–448 of the query) aligns with experimental structures 2FO0 and with kinase domain structures from both mouse and human [S26](https://search.foldseek.com/result/9iaZKGInqYU4-QKHHPSvwQ_lrqIVyLmeBHHXiA/0).

### Binding Pockets and Interfaces

The ATP-binding pocket is defined by residues 248–271 [S27](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/protein/UniProt/P00520/), and the active site by residues 359–371 [S27](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/protein/UniProt/P00520/). These regions are well-characterized in the high-resolution crystal structures. The SH3 domain (residues 61–121) contains the proline-rich peptide binding groove, experimentally validated through the 3BP-1 peptide complex [S41](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1ABO). The SH2 domain (residues 125–217) provides phosphotyrosine recognition, though no mouse SH2-peptide complex structure is listed in the provided datasets.

### Gaps and Limitations

Several important gaps exist in the structural characterization of murine ABL1. First, no experimental structure covers the C-terminal regulatory region (residues 516–1123), including the F-actin binding domain, nuclear localization signals, and the numerous phosphorylation sites in this region. Second, no full-length structure is available, limiting understanding of inter-domain communication. Third, the SH2 domain lacks an experimentally determined complex with a phosphotyrosine peptide in the mouse ortholog. Fourth, the structural basis of PIP2-mediated inhibition and myristoyl-dependent autoinhibition has not been directly visualized for the mouse protein. Fifth, the oligomeric state in solution remains unclear from crystal structures alone.

The AlphaFold models provide predictions for the disordered regions but with low confidence, and these predictions should not be interpreted as validated structures [S31](https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P00520). Similarly, sequence-based predictions of solubility (predicted soluble class with 90.6% probability), subcellular localization (ambiguous between cytoplasm and nucleus), and metal binding (predicted non-binder with 61.3% probability) [S33–S38] are computational inferences requiring experimental validation.

## 4. Interactions, expression & regulation

### Interactions, Expression & Regulation of Murine ABL1 (P00520)

### Protein Partners and Complexes

### Direct physical interactions documented in mouse

The UniProt subunit annotation for murine ABL1 (P00520) lists numerous experimentally supported interaction partners, with evidence codes distinguishing direct biochemical demonstration (ECO:0000269, PubMed-supported) from inferences based on human ortholog P00519 (ECO:0000250) [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Direct interactions established in mouse include INPPL1/SHIP2, SORBS1 (following insulin stimulation), CABLES1, PSTPIP1, ZDHHC16, and the 14-3-3 proteins YWHAB, YWHAE, YWHAG, YWHAH, SFN, and YWHAZ; the latter interactions require phosphorylation at Thr-734 and sequester ABL1 in the cytoplasm [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). A trimolecular complex containing CDK5, CABLES1, and ABL1 has been reported [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Additional direct partners include ABI1, ABI2, BCR, CRK, FYN, LYN, PSMA7, RAD9A, RAD51, RAD52, TP73, and WASF3 [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). A complex of ABL1, CTTN, and MYLK regulates cortical actin rearrangement in sphingosine 1-phosphate-mediated endothelial barrier enhancement [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). ABL1 also interacts with STX17 (probable phosphorylation substrate), ITGB1, HCK, and FGR [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). A complex containing ABL1, ABL2, CRK, and UNC119 inhibits CRK phosphorylation by ABL kinases [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). TBX21 interaction was demonstrated in mouse T cells (PubMed:21690296), and CXCL12 induces ABL1-mediated phosphorylation of NEDD9/HEF1 following their interaction (PubMed:22810897) [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520).

The crystal structure 1ABO (X-ray diffraction, 2.0 Å resolution) captures the ABL SH3 domain in complex with a synthetic peptide derived from 3BP-1 (a SH3-binding protein), providing atomic-level detail on the SH3-mediated interaction surface [S41](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1ABO). This structure involves a 62-residue ABL fragment and a 10-residue peptide, with the complex deposited as a heteromeric assembly [S41](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1ABO).

### Functional association networks (not direct binding)

STRING analysis for P00520 in mouse (species 10090) yields high-confidence functional association scores that should not be interpreted as physical binding [S29](https://string-db.org/cgi/network?identifiers=P00520&species=10090): Cbl (0.996), Crk (0.988), Bcr (0.983), Crkl (0.968), Rin1 (0.963), Atm (0.960), Pparg (0.957), Dok1 (0.944), Enah (0.933), and Abi1 (0.932). These scores integrate multiple evidence channels including co-expression, text mining, and pathway databases; the experimental score contributions range from 0.413 (Bcr) to 0.976 (Cbl), indicating that some associations are heavily supported by experimental data while others rely more on other evidence types [S29](https://string-db.org/cgi/network?identifiers=P00520&species=10090).

### Regulatory Networks and Signaling Pathways

### Activation mechanisms

ABL1 is stabilized in an inactive conformation through intramolecular associations: the SH3 domain binds the SH2-TK linker, the N-terminal cap contributes, and an N-terminal myristoyl group plus phospholipids further stabilize the autoinhibited state [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Activation occurs through autophosphorylation and SRC-family kinase-mediated phosphorylation [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). RIN1 binding to SH2 and SH3 domains activates ABL1 [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) inhibits kinase activity [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520). Imatinib mesylate (Gleevec) is a documented inhibitor [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520).

### Phosphorylation sites and their regulatory roles

- **Tyr-70**: SRC-family phosphorylation disrupts SH3-based autoinhibitory interactions and intermolecular associations (including with ABI1), enhancing kinase activity [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520)
- **Tyr-226 and Tyr-393**: phosphorylation correlates with increased activity [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520)
- **Ser-446**: phosphorylation by ATM is required for DNA damage-induced activation [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520)
- **Thr-547 and Ser-569**: attributed to a CDC2-associated kinase, coupled to cell division [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520)
- **Ser-618 and Ser-619**: PAK2 phosphorylation increases CRK binding and reduces ABI1 binding [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520)
- **Thr-734**: phosphorylation required for 14-3-3 binding and cytoplasmic sequestration [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520)
- **Lys-710**: acetylation by EP300 promotes cytoplasmic translocation [S1](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00520)
